claim_reviews.reason: Independently compared current BEHG §10 and operative draft physical page 7: €55–65 extension is explicit; premium phases are separate.
Re-read operative Articles 2–3: auction amendments and stored-fuel proof/timing provisions are present.

Current law confirms the corridor, but does not itself identify the attributed 2025 legislative choice or constitutional motivation. A contextual reading is plausible; the unresolved outcome is appropriate.

Independently read §17: the delayed-start 2027 sales price is the weighted ETS 1 allowance average from the penultimate quarter. Operational fixed quarterly sales versus auctions is a fair distinction.

Price differences are established, while private contract frequency and legal pass-through wording are not observable from legislation. Unresolved correctly preserves the commercial-practice evidentiary limit.
The independently downloaded EEX CSV contains 11 rows dated 1 July to 9 September 2026.
Independent totals are 192,084,807 certificates and €12,485,512,455. Both author roundings are correct; the 433 units left from the announced budget are immaterial.
Every official clearing-price entry equals €65. This establishes the clearing price, without implying that every submitted bid was at that price.
The independently summed bid volume is 5,181,694,753, which rounds to 5.2 billion. No rejected-bid microdata are asserted.

The independently calculated aggregate ratio is 26.976 bids per allocated certificate, with a 3.707% allocation rate. The paired inverse figures support the period-wide weighted interpretation; a different unweighted mean does not establish error.
The 1,199 bidder occurrences across 11 auctions give a mean of exactly 109. This does not count distinct firms across the entire period.

Additional primary searches did not recover the original DEHSt July report. The independently downloaded EEX data contain no bidder identities or shares. The 48% concentration figure remains unresolved.
The EEX aggregate data do not contain delivery-account types. The original DEHSt report was not recovered independently, so the 36%/64% split remains unresolved.

BEHV §12(4) and the July EEX rows confirm allocation around 21.34 million, twice the scheduled 10.67 million, all at €65. Additional allocation is deducted from the remaining annual quantity. The author specifically refers to July.

The independently downloaded ECC circular confirms collateral and limits linked to bid value. It does not identify firm size, actual credit constraints or realised net disadvantage. The unresolved outcome properly separates a plausible mechanism from measured harm.
ECC confirms forms, payments and fees, but does not quantify substantial costs for every participant or final consumer incidence. The magnitude and pass-through claims remain unresolved.

The new 20% limit per delivery account and the compliance-account condition are explicit. The July ministerial draft lacks the new §12(1 a), corroborating the earlier-version comparison. Correct the government bill locator to physical page 10.

ECC collateral follows maximum intended bid value, so reducing the permitted maximum quantity reduces the corresponding maximum collateral. This is conditional on bidding at that limit. Correct the draft locator to physical page 10.

The ECC timeline debits DCP cash one business day before auction and returns unused cash one day after. NCM margin can settle the day before or on auction day and release afterward. This supports a multi-day interval with route-specific qualifications.
New §11(1 a) deducts 40 million certificates. The rationale uses available 2025 projections because reliable 2026 data only arrive in 2028. Correct the detailed rationale locator to physical page 22.

BEHG §5 requires flexibility when the specified national quantity and EU annual-allocation conditions fail. Auction oversubscription is correctly distinguished from an actual emissions-budget shortfall.
Current and proposed §§14–15 specify €68/€70 and €73/€75. Top-up purchases take place in the following calendar year for the relevant vintage. The inventory preserves that distinction.

The annual budget plus increases minus 40 million can leave demand below the annual emissions budget but above the corridor auction volume. This conditional mechanism is supported; it does not establish duplicate charging of the same emissions.

The government rationale expressly discusses strategic bidding and temporal demand shifts. This verifies the attribution without proving effectiveness. Correct the premium-price rationale locator to physical page 23.

Cheaper early certificates create a potential gross saving. Actual incentive strength and resale behaviour depend on credit, allocation, restrictions and demand. Retaining the stronger behavioural claim as unresolved is conservative and reasonable.
Read §15: the 10% limit is calculated from certificates acquired in the preceding year, rather than emissions. The proposal covers both relevant vintages.

The complete Article 2 contains no dedicated purchase route after 31 August 2028 for corrections to old reporting years. The inventory appropriately leaves secondary-market and other legal remedies open.
Fuel quantities are linked to energy-tax declarations. Later corrections can change reported emissions and surrender obligations. This is a conditional possibility, with no asserted frequency.

Proposed §29 expressly allows 2027 certificates for emissions of 2027 or earlier years while valid. The €65 auction ceiling is below the €68/€70 premium prices. Correct the §29 locator to physical page 12.
Section 44(4) adjusts annual quantities for 2028–2030 to remove emissions leaving national scope from 2028. It does not establish an observed residual-sector share.
Read BEHV §44(1): the statutory reference period is 2016–2018. Shares are distinct from annual national totals, which can be revised. The stated historical-method premise is supported.

BEHG §7(2) establishes reporting from 2024. EBeV §§5,7 and 12 allow standard factors, individual factors and continuous measurement. The inventory correctly avoids claiming compulsory/exclusive standard values. Actual use and the degree of difference from national-inventory methods remain unresolved.

Read CO 2 KostAufG §4 against the draft BEHV and BEDV provisions: their reference periods and formulas differ as stated. Whether harmonisation is legally necessary remains a policy/legal conclusion outside this supported descriptive claim.

CO 2 KostAufG §3 requires the invoice carbon-cost component to use the applicable certificate price. This supports the need for price information for January invoices; it does not prove every supplier bills monthly or needs the requested lead time.
Read the current §4(3): publication is due by 31 March following the reporting year. BDEW proposes earlier publication; the inventory keeps current law and proposed wording separate.

Independently rendered and visually read BDEW physical page 14: added §10 is underlined and old §8 is struck out. Current CO 2 KostAufG still refers to §8. TEHG §10 governs auctions and §8 validity/transfer. The correction points in the proper direction.

Independent primary EUR-Lex extraction confirms the 17 July proposal,2031–2034 phase-in and capacity exceeding 3 t/h. This differs narrowly from inclusive 3 or more. Direct original retrieval remains challenged, and the equality case is not established as material; conservative unresolved is accepted.
BEHG §24(2)1 currently contains waste-related transition authority. The draft deletes that item while retaining annual quantity adjustment. Preserving the authority is the author’s policy request.

Read July ministerial draft physical pages 4 and 7 and TEHG §3: Emissionszertifikat means PartB/ETS 2; Berechtigung means PartA/ETS 1; §10 covers both. The residual national-sales index expressly uses Emissionszertifikaten. This supports the author’s ETS 2 label. The initial 2027 fallback to ETS 1 is a separate case. Keep the limit that current bytes are not independently timestamped historical copies.
Official EU 2026/667 Article 2 predates the July statement and moves ETS 2 operation to 2028. Earlier monitoring and early auctions are separate milestones.

July ministerial draft physical page 4 explicitly extends the €55–65 corridor to 2027, and page 1 identifies the 12 May coalition decision. The official dossier dates consultation launch 3 July. The original version concern is substantially resolved, with the current-byte historical-authenticity qualification retained.

July ministerial draft physical pages 6–7 specify overflow 68→73 and top-up 70→75 for vintage 2027. This directly verifies the referenced draft content; retain the qualification that top-up purchase occurs in the following calendar year.

Germany’s national scheme and ETS 2 delay are established. A unilateral competitive disadvantage requires matched foreign taxes, relief and process-level effective costs. Independently accessed Swedish and Irish tax material reinforces the comparison limit, without proving equal burdens.

BECV §5 allows later administrative sector recognition, so absence from the original annex cannot establish exhaustive current exclusion. An additional primary-source search did not recover the June 2026 recognition list. Unresolved accepted.
BECV recognition criteria are not a sector-specific measured risk assessment. No independent official risk evaluation for galvanising was recovered; lack of evidence does not refute the claimed risk.
ECC circular requirements establish collateral mechanics but do not compare planning or hedging opportunities of industrial SMEs and larger firms. Unresolved is appropriate.

Aid eligibility can affect cost, but the source does not measure a matched investment or competitive disadvantage for galvanisers. The underlying eligibility claim is itself unresolved. Accept the conservative outcome.

omission_audit: All 18 original physical pages re-read before inventory review. Covers, contents and boilerplate were distinguished from material premises. No additional unrecorded material factual premise was found after comparing the full original text with all 48 claims and page-based exclusions. The earlier-draft comparison of the 20% limit with the old 50% limit is now corroborated and noted in B18. Prospective passage dates, residual waste share and funding/competition forecasts remain appropriately excluded.
